rule: This map is read-only until the Wave 4 restatement. It states every non-test file outside the relation fence that still names a dying engine surface, the symbols it names, and the declared surface that answers it after the cut. Symbols are resolved from the syntax tree, not by text match, so a name that appears only in a string literal or a comment is not a read. A consumer reading only a surviving restatement target is not listed: it is already at its post-cut home. A consumer whose distinction no owner publishes carries a gap identity rather than an invented column; a gap is a finding to close in the owner, never in the consumer.

gaps.distinction: the folded query answer a reader redeems, and the publication identity it redeems it at - not the relation cell, which is now published
gaps.detail: Re-measured against the current tree. Half of what this entry named is closed and half is not, so it states both. CLOSED: the write side exists. analysis/engine/relation/runtime/snapshot publishes a terminal relation root into the canonical analysis/snapshot store - Publish seals a Projection, Project seals one family's applications as an ObservationSnapshot - and analysis/snapshot gained ExtendQuery, which appends a sealed query column to a published snapshot without advancing its generation. Rows are addressable by column identity now: Projection.Read takes a model.ColumnID and a RowKey, which is exactly what this entry said they were not. A typed read path with no engine import landed with it and is the shape the cut wants: analysis/domain/placement/relation/query.Read redeems a Placement Fact column from a Projection, decoding each cell through the OWNER's own codec and refusing the whole read on any wrong type, foreign scope, or failed decode. STILL ABSENT, and the reason these five cannot be restated: what they redeem is not a relation cell but a FOLDED QUERY ANSWER at a publication identity. All four S8 readers have one shape - snapshot.QueryPlan[identity.ContentID, engine.Answer] plus engine.AnswerValue[R] - a type-erased redemption of a domain observation such as valuedomain.ValueSummaryObservation. A projected Cell carries an opaque binding.ValueToken and a TypeID and, by the package's own declaration, 'never decodes a domain value'; only an owner holding the matching codec recovers a typed one, and what it recovers is a Fact, not a folded answer. No folded-answer column exists, and the relation side records that itself rather than substituting one: analysis/domain/placement/relation/query/summary states the typed read-only summary projection profile stays reserved and undefined 'until the upstream declaration owners publish one sealed named-role contract', because a local substitute would create a second declaration authority. The address is unpublished too: a reader keys by an owner-derived identity.ContentID over mount, point, family and context, while a Projection keys by RowKey over RelationID, RowID and witness.Scope, and no correspondence between them is published. So the answer remains a published column, in the owner, and not a rediscovery in the reader.

gaps.distinction: none - the distinction is published, by the relation-side operation instead
gaps.detail: domain/static/type_summary_observation.go exports AccumulateTypeSummary over engine.OrderedCells[TypeFact] and nothing calls it. The live fold is domain/static/relation/operation.go, whose StaticTypeSummaryOperation.Evaluate calls AccumulateTypeSummaryRows with argument.Cells. The family is bound in the corpus as StaticTypeSummary with output column static-type-summary. This entry is therefore not work for W4 but a deletion the cut can take: it is recorded because S6-domain-observation-restatement lists the file for restatement, and restating a reducer nobody calls would be work spent on residue.

Its eight siblings are all named in S3-generated-relation-owners. The typestate family is bound in the corpus, so this is a hole in the delete-set rather than an unbound judgment: the cut as written would delete every generated relation owner except this one and leave it naming a package that is gone.

gaps.detail: analysis/internal/workspace/artifact_products.go is the only surviving non-test consumer of analysis/engine/rows and rows/scalarlower. Those packages are retained under K-engine-rows as keep-if-generic, and the manifest rule is that an undischarged obligation is a delete. gaps.distinction: the thirty-seven symbols sixteen consumers read on the declared rule surface - not the way in, which now exists
gaps.detail: Re-measured against the current tree; the premise this entry was written on is spent. relcompile is no longer reachable only from the census and the laws that pin it. analysis/program/relationadmission/admission.go imports it in non-test production code and binds a checked certificate to the owner-issued logical inventory that witness.Specialize consumes, and analysis/schema/rule/relcompile/authorityprojection/project.go imports it as well. That is the entry point this entry said no manifest entry built. What remains is the measurement that made this a gap in the first place, and it is unchanged: of the thirty-seven symbols the sixteen entries naming relcompile as their target read, relcompile declares none, and every one of them is declared in analysis/engine and nowhere else. So no partial move exists and the sixteen still wait - not on a way in, which landed, but on the declared surface publishing what they read.

gaps.distinction: the four consumers' admission and answer symbols on the relational runtime - not the runtime, which now exists
gaps.detail: Re-measured against the current tree; the premise this entry was written on is spent. The runtime is no longer one doc.go. analysis/engine/relation/runtime declares Solve(mounted, base, view) returning a terminal.Result, and carries the snapshot and terminal subpackages beside it. It is reached from production, not only from laws: analysis/program/relationadmission/runtime/solve.go and cmd/relparity/corpusprobe/new.go both import it in non-test code. So S1-analyzer-constructor no longer restates onto a stub. What remains is narrower and is why the four entries still wait. The runtime declares none of the symbols they read - CommittedProgram and Answer are declared in analysis/engine and nowhere else - so the surface those consumers move onto is the runtime's published answer, which it does not yet expose under those identities. The gap is the missing declaration, no longer a missing package.

gaps.distinction: the payload an unwritten coordinate carries, and the read contract that decides it
gaps.detail: Measured on real fixtures with both surfaces driven for real, not read off signatures. The engine observation and the relational binding's span deliver a row as the same three results - value, present, available - and they agree on a written coordinate and disagree on an unwritten one. Under ReadSparseExplicit an unwritten coordinate arrives from the engine as the owner's DECLARED DEFAULT with present=false: semantic.Domain.PartitionKey and JoinUnderKey stamp domain.ops.Default into the factbinding entry, and execution.ReadCellPolicy.Cell passes it through verbatim. relbindgen's Span.At returns the Go zero instead - frame.go answers (var zero T, false, true) for any presence that is neither Present nor AuthenticatedOpaque - and Members.Fill carries that zero into the operand vector a reducer takes. On every axis measured the two are different values: heap Value{} is neither Valid nor Bottom while the axis default is Bottom; placement Fact{} equals BottomFact() while the axis default is DefaultFact(){Stack,Refuted}; static TypeFact{} is not Valid while the axis default is TypeBottom. The consequence is live in this tree. PlacementContainmentOperation.Evaluate fills its placement vector through Members.Fill and folds it with containment.ContainmentFold, which authenticates the parent cell through placement.AuthenticateFactCell - and that admits an unwritten cell only as exactly DefaultFact(). A Go-zero absent cell is refused there, so the binding refuses a row the engine admits. placement.buildStaticHeapGraphRows refuses the same way, on !value.Valid() and again on (!present && !value.IsBottom()), its own comment stating that no sparse payload other than the owner's Bottom is admissible. domain/static's and domain/value's summary folds skip an absent cell without inspecting its payload and are therefore blind to the difference, which is why the corpus can certify while the distinction is unpublished. Two further clauses of the same contract have no delivered form at all: ReadSparseFactorDefault, under which the engine delivers an unwritten coordinate as the default and PRESENT so a fold has no absent branch to get wrong, and ReadOrderByTag with its refusal of duplicate tags. The answer is for the delivered span to publish the owner's sparse payload and its read contract. A fold re-deriving a default its owner already declared is the rediscovery this map exists to refuse.
